newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper won't resign, official says.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper won't resign, official says.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper has no intention of leaving office before his term ends in August 1998, his right-hand man Interior Minister Horacio Serpa said on Friday.
"There won't be any resignation by the president of the republic," Serpa told reporters.
"It's naive to suggest it," he said of calls for the embattled Samper to step down. "It does nothing to help overcome the countless problems our country is suffering from."
Serpa's comments in the northern oil producing centre of Barrancabermeja came after two leading Colombian newspapers called on Samper to resign for the good of the country.
El Colombiano of Medellin, the country's second-largest daily, said Colombians had endured Samper "incompetence" long enough and his departure was the only solution to the country's woes.
On Thursday, Bogota's El Espectador newspaper described Samper as "an unburied corpse" and said his leadership, or lack of it, had brough Colombia to "the brink of an abyss."

Both newspapers urged Samper to resign on several occasions last year, at the height of the political crisis stemming from charges that he used millions of dollars in Cali cartel drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.

El Colombiano said its latest call was based, at least in part, on the likelihood that Colombia will remain on a virtual U.S. blacklist of countries that have failed to cooperate in the war on drugs as long as Samper remains in office.
Last year, U.S. President Bill Clinton "decertified" Colombia and cut U.S. economic aid to the country, a move many Colombians blamed on Samper's drug-tainted image.
